newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria Social Democrat support plunges - poll.
newsitem.headline: Austria Social Democrat support plunges - poll.

text.p: Support for Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats has dropped seven percent since December with voters turning to the far right, leftist Greens and liberals, an opinion poll said on Thursday.

The survey conducted by the Gallup Institute for weekly current affairs magazine News showed backing for the Social Democrats at one of its lowest levels since 1945 at 31 percent compared to the 38 percent it won in December's general election.

The nationwide poll, carried out ahead of Austria's first European parliamentary elections on October 13, gave the nationalist Freedom Party led by populist Joerg Haider 25 percent, up three points since December.

Haider, who has called for a renegotiation of the large net payments Austria makes to European Union coffers, has set out to tap voter dissatisfaction over EU membership, in particular among farmers and low-paid workers. Austria joined the EU in January last year.
But some 46 percent of 500 voters surveyed said they had yet to decide which party to back.
The conservative People's Party (OeVP), the junior partner in the coalition government with Social Democrats, remained steady on 28 percent, the Gallup poll showed.
Support for the Greens almost doubled to nine percent from 4.8 percent in the last general election, while the Liberal Forum party received seven percent backing, up from 5.5 percent.
